# Workflow automation without APIs

Wexpro Labs explains how to evaluate browser, desktop, legacy-interface, file, and API steps in one reviewed workflow when a complete API integration does not exist.

## Short answer

Use an API when it reliably exposes the needed data or action. Evaluate browser, desktop, legacy-interface, or file steps when that is where the real work happens and the intended result can be verified. Keep consequential actions outside automated scope unless a separate review mechanism is implemented and verified. Stop uncertain cases instead of guessing.

## Fit criteria

- Repeatable workflow with a recognizable routine path.
- Known checks and an observable completed result.
- Multiple systems, files, or handoffs that a single integration does not cover.
- An explicit boundary that keeps consequential approval or judgment with a person.
- A measurable manual baseline, completion rate, review time, and cost per completed case.

## Boundaries

Do not automate undocumented judgment, unstable interfaces with no detectable failure signal, or consequential actions with no safe review point. A controlled pilot should establish the real baseline before volume increases.
